starting_head_subject: content(P2): add character and monster product projections

public_api.name_ambiguity_note: ContentProductService.get_stage / get_encounter return PRODUCT documents; ContentDatabase.get_stage / get_encounter return the raw canonical entity envelope. Both methods document the distinction in their docstrings.

enumeration_authority.allow_list: ContentDatabase.ENUMERABLE_ENTITY_TABLES == ("avatars", "monsters", "stages", "encounters"); anything outside it raises ContentDatabaseError
enumeration_authority.ordering: deterministic numeric-aware ascending; encounter IDs are colon-composite so they use a per-segment numeric-aware key (a plain numeric key would sort "maze:1000" before "maze:999")
enumeration_authority.product_layer: the product layer calls only database.list_stage_ids()/list_encounter_ids() and contains no sqlite3 import, no database_path access, no SQL keyword and no storage table name
enumeration_authority.nanoka_content_diff: 13 insertions, 1 deletion -- the single deletion is the widened ENUMERABLE_ENTITY_TABLES constant; no existing query output moved

stage_package_reuse_policy.rule: get_stage_package(...) is the SOLE topology authority. The Stage product PRESERVES it and never rebuilds it.

rule_metadata_policy.note: win/lose conditions are opaque stage-authored tokens; they are never converted into ScenarioCompiler rule identifiers

monster_placements.requested_monster_id: preserved verbatim (never normalised into the canonical parent)

representation: field_values (null when the record supplies no value)
f9_retained_fields.non_interpretation_statement: these three are carried verbatim as static/source metadata and are never read as runtime behavior

f10_mode_policy.encounter_source_modes: game-mode context exists only at Encounter level: boss / maze / story
f10_mode_policy.explicit_statement: stage_type 'Challenge' must never be read as an established game mode; no canonical gameplay mode (Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, Apocalyptic Shadow, ...) is inferred or claimed
f10_mode_policy.separation: raw_stage_type and encounter_source_modes are exposed as separate fields and are never merged

encounter_representation.static_context: the whole payload copied verbatim, plus common_fields_present / mode_context_fields_present / unrecognised_fields / context_fields_present / context_merged_across_encounters
encounter_representation.related_stages: the payload's own stage_id, cross-checked with get_stage for existence; order_supplied=false because the record supplies no ordering
encounter_representation.unknown_fields: anything outside the common and expected mode sets is surfaced as unrecognised_fields rather than dropped

locale_policy.finding: Stage and Encounter records carry NO en/ja/ko/zh locale bundle, unlike avatars and monsters
locale_policy.stage_name: an INT for all 1,459 stages -- a static numeric identifier, not a display string (stage_name_kind = STATIC_NUMERIC_ID)
locale_policy.note: the exact static text supplied is reported verbatim and no localization is fabricated

determinism_copy_policy.hash: every document carries product_sha256 = stable_hash(document without the hash field)
determinism_copy_policy.ordering: all collections explicitly sorted; stage IDs numeric-aware, encounter IDs per-segment numeric-aware
determinism_copy_policy.representation: plain dict documents; immutable typing explicitly NOT claimed
determinism_copy_policy.copy_isolation: every returned document and summary row is deepcopy-isolated
determinism_copy_policy.browse_cost_decision: list_stages() is driven by get_stage + one encounter pass and does NOT call get_stage_package per row; the four package-derived counts are opt-in via include_package_topology and are explicitly null by default rather than guessed or re-derived

package_authority_cross_check.note: topology.package_sha256 re-derived from get_stage_package on a deterministic sample

data_facts_recorded: every packaged 4.4.54 Stage has exactly ONE wave -- this is a data fact, not a schema limitation
every Encounter relates to exactly ONE Stage (0 multi-stage encounters)
446 Stages contain at least one variant-only (MONSTER_VARIANT) Monster placement
